facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026 lists the Health Management Information System, which it describes as routinely providing service and disease indicators, first among the subsystems coordinated within the Ministry of Health; the statement is undated, so the revision date of February 2023 is used.

The National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026, costed at ZMW 158.3 billion over five years, names the HMIS as a basis for monitoring the plan and sets an intervention to strengthen compatibility and integration of health information systems at different levels (cHMIS, DHMIS, HMIS, eLMIS), to be carried out through a Digital Health strategic plan then being developed; revision date of February 2023 used.

Among the challenges of the HIV programme the National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026 lists that the Health Management Information System for HIV prevention 'is still paper based'; the statement covers that programme's reporting only, not the HMIS as a whole, and is undated, so the revision date of February 2023 is used.

The National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026 names SmartCare, an electronic system capturing individual patient-level information on various illnesses, says it was re-engineered during 2017-2021 to be web-based and usable at all levels, and places health information interventions under a Digital Health strategic plan then being developed; it sets no SmartCare coverage figure in the passages read; revision date of February 2023 used.

systems.tiers: intended for 'all levels'; none stated as in use

note: Passages only. DHIS2 appears in the acronym list alone and is not tied to the HMIS in the passages read.
